product: NASA PGDA product 69: LOLA-derived average illumination and Earth visibility, south pole 85-90 S, 60 m
citation: Mazarico, E., et al. (2011), Illumination conditions of the lunar polar regions using LOLA topography, Icarus, 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030

meaning.sunShort: average share of the Sun’s disc in view
meaning.earthShort: share of hours; counts as visible if any part of its disc shows
meaning.basis: averaged over hourly steps spanning 18.6 years
meaning.sun: Average fraction of the solar disc in view, over hourly timesteps spanning 18.6 years (one lunar nutation cycle): the label's "average illumination by the solar disc" and "average solar disc visibility".
meaning.earth: Earth: visible if any part of its disc is not obscured (NASA notes this is slightly optimistic for radio links); the share of hourly timesteps over 18.6 years in which it was.
meaning.labelConflict: Both labels' longer DESCRIPTION also says the values "indicate the percentage of timesteps where each pixel was sunlit (by any fraction of the solar disc)" (Earth label: "of the Earth disc", "sunlit" kept). For the Sun this differs from the title, the column description and the product page; the card uses the latter.

grid.crs: Moon2000_spole: polar stereographic, latitude of origin -90, central meridian 0, sphere

copy.note: A crop of the full map, centred on the pole. Original int16 values, nothing resampled.
copy.tileLayout: gzip of: Sun layer then Earth layer; each layer is tilePx x tilePx int16 cells, rows from the top (grid +y), stored as row-wise differences (first cell of a row as is, each other cell minus the cell to its left, wrapping in 16 bits), all low bytes then all high bytes
